library(dplyr); library(ggplot2); library(gt); library(scales)

scored_path <- "data/backtest_scored.rds"
meta_path   <- "data/backtest_meta.rds"
scored <- if (file.exists(scored_path)) readRDS(scored_path) else NULL
meta   <- if (file.exists(meta_path))   readRDS(meta_path)   else NULL
has_backtest <- !is.null(scored) && nrow(scored) > 0L

## Methodology

For each historical as-of date $T$ on a quarterly grid:

1. Read ABS NOM as it stood at $T$ from the captured vintage history
   when one exists (weekly snapshots since May 2026); otherwise fall
   back to today's values restricted by the documented publication lag
   (~183 days). OAD (~35 days) and visa grants (~45 days) are always
   today's values restricted by lag.
2. Aggregate monthly OAD to quarters. The quarter just completed at $T$
   has only one of its three months published, so it is grossed up
   using each month's historical share of its quarter rather than
   summed as if complete (see *Data completeness at the live edge* on
   the Methodology page).
3. Refit every model from scratch on this restricted panel.
4. Score predictions at horizons $h \in \{-2, -1, 0, +1\}$ quarters
   relative to $T$, where $h = 0$ is the quarter just completed at $T$
   (NOM not yet published) and $h = -2, -1$ are recent backcasts.
5. Use the latest available ABS NOM as the evaluation "truth", and —
   for origins with a real vintage — the ABS value first published for
   that quarter as the preliminary benchmark.

Origins before the first captured vintage are therefore
**pseudo-real-time** (today's values, lag-restricted); later origins
are genuinely vintage-aware. The run details below say how many
origins used a real vintage.

Models compared:

| Model | What it uses |
|-------|--------------|
| `bayes_headline` | **Phase 3 v0.1.** Same trivariate observation structure as `kalman_multi_v2` but fit via HMC in Stan, so the credible intervals come from proper posterior sampling instead of treating MLE parameters as fixed. Headline-only. Only fit on the last `cfg$models$bayes_headline$backtest_window` (default 12) quarters of the backtest grid. |
| `bayes_gamma`    | **Phase 3 v0.2.** Extends `bayes_headline` with a Gamma-weighted forward lag from visa grants to arrivals (matches `kalman_v4`'s parametric Gamma lag). The visa observation row loads on `log_sum_exp` of future latent log-arrivals weighted by a fixed Gamma(α, β) pmf. Backtest window same as `bayes_headline`. |
| `bayes_gamma_learned` | **Phase 3 v0.3.** Same architecture as `bayes_gamma` but the Gamma shape and rate (α, β) are sampled jointly with the rest of the model instead of pinned from config. The kalman v5 grid-search becomes proper HMC marginalisation, and the credible intervals on `nom_hat` include lag-shape uncertainty. |
| `bayes_kalman`        | **Phase 3 v0.6.** Same observation streams as `bayes_gamma` but the latent state trajectory is integrated out analytically via a forward Kalman filter inside the Stan model. Only ~10 static parameters are sampled, vs ~400 in the latent-state versions, which eliminates the σ_oad ↔ σ_mu identifiability funnel — diagnostics go from 60-99% treedepth saturation to 0, ESS rises 10×. Two model trade-offs: the `log_sum_exp` visa equation is linearised to a weighted sum of log-arrivals, and the Gamma lag is backward in calendar (visa at t informs arrivals at t..t-K) rather than forward like `bayes_gamma`. |
| `kalman_multi_v2` | Multivariate Kalman: OAD + visa grants + NOM as joint observations on a shared latent log-arrivals state. Phase 2 v4.0 with Gamma-lag state augmentation. |
| `kalman_multi_pi` | Same multi-SSM fit, but headline assembled via the empirical-π route instead of the direct NOM observation. |
| `kalman_v1` | Phase 1 univariate Kalman per category, π-based headline. |
| `bridge` | OLS bridge regression: NOM ~ lagged OAD + lagged visa grants. |
| `random_walk` | Headline NOM at $T-1$ rolled forward. |
| `ar1` | AR(1) on quarter-on-quarter NOM growth. |
| `abs_preliminary` | The ABS NOM value as first published, scored against the latest vintage. Only populated for origins that have a captured vintage; empty (shown as —) for pseudo-real-time origins. |

The backtest is computed offline (via `scripts/refresh_backtest.R`)
and the scored tibble is committed to the repo. The site renders cheaply
on every push; the backtest refreshes on demand or on a slower cadence.

## Headline results

```{r headline-table}
#| eval: !expr has_backtest
has_calib <- all(c("cov80", "cov95") %in% names(scored))
agg <- scored |>
  dplyr::filter(category == "total") |>
  dplyr::group_by(model, horizon) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n      = sum(n,   na.rm = TRUE),
    RMSE   = mean(rmse, na.rm = TRUE),
    MAE    = mean(mae,  na.rm = TRUE),
    Bias   = mean(bias, na.rm = TRUE),
    RMSEp  = mean(rmse_vs_prelim, na.rm = TRUE),
    LogS   = mean(log_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Cov80  = if (has_calib) mean(cov80, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    Cov95  = if (has_calib) mean(cov95, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(RMSE)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(horizon, RMSE) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Horizon = paste0("h = ", horizon),
                RMSEp = ifelse(is.finite(RMSEp), RMSEp, NA_real_)) |>
  dplyr::select(Horizon, Model = model, n, RMSE, MAE, Bias, RMSEp, LogS, Cov80, Cov95)

agg |>
  gt::gt(groupname_col = "Horizon") |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = c("RMSE", "MAE", "Bias", "RMSEp"),
                 decimals = 0, use_seps = TRUE) |>
  gt::fmt_number(columns = "LogS", decimals = 2) |>
  gt::fmt_percent(columns = c("Cov80", "Cov95"), decimals = 0) |>
  gt::sub_missing(missing_text = "—") |>
  gt::cols_label(RMSEp = "RMSE vs ABS prelim", LogS = "Log score",
                 Cov80 = "80% cov", Cov95 = "95% cov") |>
  gt::tab_options(table.font.size = "small") |>
  gt::tab_source_note(gt::md(
    paste0(
      "Backtest grid: ",
      if (!is.null(meta)) meta$n_successful else "?",
      " of ",
      if (!is.null(meta)) meta$n_asof_dates else "?",
      " quarterly as-of dates",
      if (!is.null(meta)) paste0(" from ",
            nn_quarter_label(meta$grid_from, sep = "-"), " to ",
            nn_quarter_label(meta$grid_to,   sep = "-"))
      else "",
      ". Refreshed ",
      if (!is.null(meta)) format(meta$refreshed_at, "%d %B %Y") else "—",
      ". RMSE / MAE / Bias in persons, against the latest ABS vintage. ",
      "**RMSE vs ABS prelim** scores against the value ABS first published for the quarter; only origins with a captured vintage contribute, so it is blank for most models and horizons until the vintage history is longer. ",
      "**Log score** is the average per-observation log-likelihood of the truth under the model's predictive distribution (higher is better — proper scoring rule). ",
      "**Cov80 / Cov95** are the empirical coverage of the model's 80% / 95% credible intervals; well-calibrated models should sit at 80% / 95%. ",
      "Models are sorted within each horizon by RMSE."
    )
  ))
```

## Calibration

How often does the truth actually fall inside each model's 80% and
95% credible intervals? A well-calibrated model should have an 80%
interval that contains the truth 80% of the time, and similarly
for 95%. Materially below those targets means the model is
overconfident; materially above means the intervals are too wide
(under-confident).

```{r calibration-plot}
#| eval: !expr has_backtest
library(ggplot2)
calib <- scored |>
  dplyr::filter(category == "total", is.finite(cov80) | is.finite(cov95)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(model, horizon) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cov80 = mean(cov80, na.rm = TRUE),
                   cov95 = mean(cov95, na.rm = TRUE),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c("cov80", "cov95"),
                      names_to = "interval", values_to = "coverage") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    nominal  = ifelse(interval == "cov80", 0.80, 0.95),
    interval = ifelse(interval == "cov80", "80%", "95%")
  )
ggplot(calib, aes(x = horizon, y = coverage, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = nominal), linetype = 2, colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_line(aes(group = model)) +
  facet_wrap(~ interval, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = -2:1) +
  labs(x = "Horizon (quarters from as-of date)",
       y = "Empirical coverage",
       title = "Credible-interval calibration",
       subtitle = "Dashed line is the nominal coverage (target).") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.title = element_blank())
```

## Notes on interpretation

- **Bridge regression dominates backcasts** (h = -2, -1) because it
  regresses NOM directly on lagged flows with no log-Gaussian
  assumption baggage. Its h = 0 RMSE looks worst because at the
  current-quarter horizon many of its regressors are missing (OAD
  publication lag) and `predict()` returns NA for those rows. Those
  NAs propagate to a few large errors.
- The **multivariate Kalman** is the recommended production model
  because it gives unified uncertainty quantification across all
  horizons and produces credible intervals on the headline. Bridge
  regression doesn't natively give intervals on out-of-sample
  forecasts.
- **No model has direct NOM signal at h = 0 / h = +1** (NOM isn't
  published yet at those horizons), so all Kalman variants converge
  to similar performance. This is the structural limit of point
  estimation from public data.
- **Before October 2026 every model showed a large one-signed h = 0
  under-prediction** (−53k to −98k post-COVID). That was a data
  construction artefact, not a modelling result: the quarter just
  completed at each origin had only one of its three OAD months
  published and was summed as if complete, so every model was told
  arrivals had collapsed by two thirds. The panel now grosses partial
  quarters up by historical month shares; snapshots refreshed after
  that fix are not comparable with earlier published numbers.
- **The ABS preliminary "model"** is only populated for origins that
  have a captured vintage (weekly since May 2026), so it is sparse for
  now and grows one quarter per ABS release. For earlier origins there
  is no preliminary value and the column is blank.
- **The random walk has no h = 0 / h = +1 entry** by construction: with
  a ~6-month NOM lag the previous quarter's NOM is not yet published
  at the origin either.

## Run details

```{r run-meta}
if (!is.null(meta)) {
  cat(sprintf("- Backtest as-of dates: %d (%s to %s)\n",
              meta$n_asof_dates,
              as.character(meta$grid_from),
              as.character(meta$grid_to)))
  if (!is.null(meta$n_real_vintage_origins)) {
    cat(sprintf("- Origins with a real NOM vintage: %d\n", meta$n_real_vintage_origins))
  }
  if (!is.null(meta$models)) {
    cat(sprintf("- Models in snapshot:   %s\n", paste(meta$models, collapse = ", ")))
  }
  if (!is.null(meta$oad_partial_quarter)) {
    cat(sprintf("- Partial OAD quarters: %s\n", meta$oad_partial_quarter))
  }
  cat(sprintf("- Last refreshed:       %s\n",
              format(meta$refreshed_at, "%d %B %Y %H:%M %Z")))
} else {
  cat("- No backtest snapshot present yet.\n")
}
cat(sprintf("- Site build:           %s\n",
            format(Sys.time(), "%d %B %Y %H:%M %Z")))
```
